info.bio:
Bonnie Lynn Raitt, (8 de noviembre de 1949, Burbank (California), Estados Unidos) es una cantante y guitarrista de Blues y R&B, hija de la estrella de musicales de Broadway John Raitt.

Raitt comenzó a tocar la guitarra a una edad muy temprana, algo que no hacían muchas de sus amigas del colegio. Más tarde se hizo famosa por su estilo de tocar la guitarra con slide.

En 1967, Raitt continuó su carrera entrando en el Radcliffe College para estudiar una licenciatura en estudios africanos.

Un día un amigo le dijo que el productor de blues Dick Waterman daba una entrevista en la WHRB, la emisora del Harvard College. Raitt fue a verlo, y rápidamente se hicieron amigos. Cuando Waterman se trasladó a Philadelphia con sus músicos y amigos, Bonnie Raitt estaba entre ellos formando una parte muy activa. Por entonces tocaba folk y R&B en clubs de Boston, llegando a tocar junto a figuras como Howlin' Wolf, Sippie Wallace, y Mississippi Fred McDowell, todos conocidos a través de Waterman

En los últimos años de los 70, un periodista del NewsWeek Magazine la vio en concierto junto a Fred McDowell, y numerosos cazatalentos empezaron a frecuentar sus actuaciones. Finalmente aceptó una oferta con la Warner Bros., quienes le dieron la oportunidad de sacar su primer disco homónimo. Fue una de las primeras mujeres en ser reconocidas como gran guitarrista, sobre todo por su técnica de slide. en 1972 sacó un nuevo disco, Give It Up, intentando mejorar el modesto éxito que tuvo el anterior. Aunque tuvo buenas críticas, el éxito comercial tardaba en llegar, y lo mismo pasó con su tercer album Takin' My Time. A pesar de llegar a tener un titular en la revista Rolling Stone incluso, Bonnie Raitt decidió experimentar con nuevos sonidos para su nuevo album Streetlights de 1974, y tomó un nuevo estilo mas blues en 1975 con su disco Home Plate. Realizó una colaboración en el disco homónimo de Warren Zevon con amigos como Jackson Browne, Lindsey Buckingham y Stevie Nicks.

En 1977 publica Sweet Forgiveness, que le da su escape al éxito comercial con un éxito llamado Runaway, versión de Del Shannon. Esta versión llamó la atención de Columbia Records, que comenzó las negociaciones con Warner Bros. Tras la gran expectación de su nuevo album The Glow, pero tuvo modestas ventas y peores críticas. Comenzó a oirse su nombre cuanco colaboró en la organización de los 5 conciertos de MUSE (Musicos unidos para el ahorro energético) en el Madison Square Garden. Hasta 1982 no lanzó su siguiente album, Green Light, que tuvo un gran éxito para la crítica pero seguía sin convencer al gran público, con lo que Warner decidió terminar el contrato.

En 1983, Warner Bros hizo una criba de artistas, entre los que cayeron Van Morrison, Arlo Guthrie y Bonnie Raitt. Por entonces, ella estaba trabajando en un nuevo album titulado Tonge & Groove, y la falta de apoyo para terminarlo la empujó a caer en la adicción del alcohol y las drogas.

Aparte de sus problemas personales y profesionales, Raitt continuaba de gira y participaba activamente en la política internacional. En 1985 cantó junto a multitud de artisas en el video de Sun City que se dedicó a la lucha contra el apartheid. También colaboró en el Farm Aid, en muchos conciertos de Amnistía Internacional y en el concierto sovietico/americano de Moscú por la Paz, emitido por televisión. Junto a Don Henley, Herbie Hancock y Holly Near colaboró en el concierto contra el SIDA de 1987.

Dos años más tarde de que fuera despedida de Warner Bros., le notifican que tienen planes de lanzar su disco, con el título de Nine Lives. Su éxito fue nulo, tanto para crítica como para el público. A finales de 1987 se unió a KD lang y a Jennifer Warnes para un epecial de Roy Orbison para televisión. Por entonces Raitt ya estaba desintoxicada y sobria, dicen que gracias a Stevie Ray Vaughn. A punto estuvo de firmar para Paisley Park, cuando recibió una suculenta oferta de Capitol Records. Su primera aportación fue una version de Baby Mine, de Dumbo, para un recopilatorio tributo a Disney, y comenzó a trabajar en nuevo material.

En su décimo album, Nick of Time, consiguió colocar un número 1 en las listas americanas y ganó 3 Grammys, mientras ganaba un cuarto por su dueto con John Lee Hooker en la canción In the Mood. Su siguiente album Luck of the Draw ganó 3 Grammys más, y dio una de las mejores baladas de todos los tiempos, "I Can't Make You Love Me". Un nuevo álbum en 1994 llamado Longing in Their Hearts le dio dos nuevos Grammys, llegando incluso al disco de platino las ventas. Terminó la decada de los 90 con su disco Fundamental.

scenes.name: Country-rock y roots-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En los setenta, el reajuste a los viejos valores (blues, folk, country) convierte al rock en uno de los mayores éxitos del consumismo: el Establishment ya no intenta destruirlo, lo absorbe. El country-rock de Gram Parsons es una moda enorme: Commander Cody, New Riders Of The Purple Sage, Manassas, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Poco y los Eagles (Desperado, Hotel California); en Nashville surgen los «outlaws» (Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Kris Kristofferson). El roots-rock sigue con Hot Tuna, Little Feat y Doobie Brothers, y la nostalgia recupera el blues (Roy Buchanan, Bonnie Raitt), la armonía vocal (Manhattan Transfer, Roches, McGarrigle Sisters) y los cincuenta (American Graffiti).

podcast.title: Career Reboot - Grammy Win (1990)
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt's career underwent a dramatic transformation after her "Nick of Time" album won Album of the Year at the 1990 Grammy Awards, marking her as the "recording Academy's best Cinderella story." Prior to this, she had been toiling since the early 70s without a top 40 pop hit or top 20 LP, battling drug and alcohol addiction, from which she got sober in the late 80s. The Grammy win rebooted her career, turning her into a pop star at age 40, leading to consistent top 20 album chart placements and top 40 hits throughout the 90s. "You can literally divide Bonnie Rates' career into before she won the Grammy and after she won the Grammy."

podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt inducted her friend John Prine into the Songwriter's Hall of Fame in 2019. "John Prine was inducted into the song writer's Hall of Fame in 2019, inducted by his friend, Bonnie Raid."

podcast.title: Accolades and Career Achievements
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt has enjoyed a long and successful solo career, earning 10 Grammy Awards and induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. She has also performed with numerous other notable artists. "Bonnie has had a long and successful solo career. I mean, 10 Grammy Awards. She's in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Advocacy and Philanthropy for Artists
podcast.body: In 1988, Bonnie Raitt co-founded the Rhythm and Blues Foundation, an organization dedicated to improving royalty payments for artists. She further demonstrated her commitment to music education by donating the profits from her special Fender signature Stratocaster to the Bonnie Raitt Guitar Project, which assists underprivileged youth in playing music. "In 1988, she co-founded the Rhythm and Blues Foundation, an organization dedicated to improving the royalty payments made to artists."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alcohol Abuse Impact
podcast.body: Her life and career were made significantly more complicated by her alcohol abuse, influenced by her desire to fit into the male-dominated blues scene. "Her life and presumably her career was made much more complicated by her alcohol abuse."

podcast.title: Career Trajectory of Producer Don Was
podcast.body: Don Was described his own career change from being a "pariah as a record producer to being in demand" after working with Bonnie Raitt, indicating a significant turning point in his professional life that he was still "surfing that wave" of 35-40 years later. "I went through it a little bit with Bonnie and Bonnie wasn't the artist. I went from like not going from being a pariah as a record producer to being in demand."

podcast.title: Emulating Male Blues Artists' Lifestyle
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt admitted she wanted to be the "female version of Muddy Waters" and bought into the lifestyle of drinking to prove she could "hold my liquor" with professional blues drinkers, viewing figures like Keith Richards as cool and dangerous. This behavior, however, led to her being dropped by Warner Records. "I wanted to be the female version of Muddy Waters. There was a real man's about drinking and doing blues."

podcast.title: Included on List of Guitar Heroes
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt is mentioned as an artist who should be included on the list of significant guitar players. "We can probably include Bonnie Rate on this list too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Live Performance with Roy Orbison
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt participated in Roy Orbison's live TV special "A Black and White Night," performing as a backing singer and musician out of admiration for him. "He got inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and recorded a live TV special, a black and white night, where he was joined by Elvis's 70s backing band, Bruce Springsteen, Elvis Costello, K.D. Lang, Bunny Raite, Jackson Brown and Tom Wait, among others, while just acting as backing singers and musicians for a man they admired."

podcast.title: Marketing Challenges as a Blues Artist
podcast.body: Record companies in the 1970s struggled to market blues artists, and this was particularly true for Bonnie Raitt, who was fundamentally a blues musician. Her label, Warner Records, did not effectively promote her work. "Record companies had no idea how to market blues artists in the 1970s. So for Bonnie Raight, a member of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and one of the greatest slide guitar players ever, and who is at her very core a blues artist, well, no company, record company is going to have the desire or be the clue to know what to do with her."

podcast.title: Recognition as a Top Guitarist and Slide Player
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt was included in Rolling Stone's 2011 list of the 100 Greatest Guitarists of All Time and Gibson's 2014 list of the top 10 female guitarists. She is uniquely distinguished in this discussion as the only guitarist who plays slide, a technique central to her blues-infused style. "Bonnie is the only guitarist we've talked about who plays Slide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction
podcast.body: Bonnie Raitt is a member of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, recognized for her contributions as one of the greatest slide guitar players. "So for Bonnie Raight, a member of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and one of the greatest slide guitar players ever, and who is at her very core a blues artist, well, no company, record company is going to have the desire or be the clue to know what to do with her."

podcast.title: Sobriety and Label Change (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, Bonnie Raitt battled and overcame drug and alcohol addiction, getting sober, and subsequently signed with a new label, Capital Records, just before the release of her career-defining album "Nick of Time." "She had battled drug and alcohol addiction, got sober in the late 80s and signed to a new label, Capital Records."

xref.title: Retirement and Posthumous Recognition
xref.body: After decades of recording numerous songs, her declining health in the 1950s, including a series of strokes that impaired her ability to play guitar, forced her to retire. She passed away in a nursing home in 1973, but in 1996, Bonnie Raitt funded a headstone for her, inscribed with an epitaph praising her singular contribution to the blues. "A series of strokes destroyed her ability to play guitar, and she died in a nursing home in 1973."
